==Problem==
A team of students is going to compete against a team of teachers in a trivia contest. The total number of students and teachers is <imath>15</imath>. Ash, a cousin of one of the students, wants to join the contest. If Ash plays with the students, the average age on that team will increase from <imath>12</imath> to <imath>14.</imath> If Ash plays with the teachers, the average age on that team will decrease from <imath>55</imath> to <imath>52</imath>. How old is Ash?

<imath>\textbf{(A)}~28\qquad\textbf{(B)}~29\qquad\textbf{(C)}~30\qquad\textbf{(D)}~32\qquad\textbf{(E)}~33</imath>

==Solution 1 ==

When Ash joins a team, the team's average is pulled towards his age. Let <imath>A</imath> be Ash's age and <imath>N</imath> be the number of people on the student team. This means that there are <imath>15-N</imath> people in the teacher team. Let us write an expression for the change in the average for each team.

The students originally had an average of <imath>12</imath>, which became <imath>14</imath> when Ash joined, so there was an increase of <imath>2</imath>. The term <imath>A-12</imath> represents how much older Ash is compared to the average of the students'. If we divide this by <imath>N+1</imath>, which is the number of people on the student team when Ash joins, we get the average change per team member once Ash is added. Therefore, 
<cmath>\frac{A-12}{N+1} = 2.</cmath>

Similarly, for teachers, the average was originally <imath>55</imath>, which decreased by <imath>3</imath> to become <imath>52</imath> when Ash joined. Intuitively, <imath>55-A</imath> represents how much younger Ash is than the average age of the teachers. Dividing this by the expression <imath>(15-N)+1</imath>, which is the new total number of people on the teacher team, represents the average change per team member once Ash joins. We can write the equation

<cmath> \frac{55-A}{16-N} = 3.</cmath>

To solve the system, multiply equation (1) by <imath>N+1</imath>, and similarly multiply equation (2) by <imath>16-N</imath>. Then add the equations together, canceling <imath>A</imath>, leaving equation <imath>43=50-N</imath>. From this we get <imath>N=7</imath> and <imath>A= \boxed{28}.</imath>

~lprado

==Solution 2==

As shown above, we get the equation <cmath> \frac{55-A}{16-N} = 3.</cmath> Rearranging we get <cmath> \frac{55-A}{3} = 16-N.</cmath> Therefore, since N must be an integer, <imath>55-A</imath> must be divisible by 3. Plugging in values gets us <imath>A= \boxed{28}.</imath>

==Solution 3==

Another way is to say that there are <imath>S</imath> students and <imath>T</imath> teachers and Ash's age is <imath>A</imath>. We can create the equations
\begin{align}
&(1) S+T=15 \\
&(2) \frac{12S+A}{S+1}=14 \\ 
&(3) \frac{55T+A}{T+1}=52
\end{align}
Equation <imath>(2)</imath> simplifies to <imath>A=2S+14</imath> and equation <imath>(3)</imath> simplifies to <imath>A=-3T+52</imath>. Multiply equation <imath>(2)</imath> by <imath>3</imath> to get equation \begin{align} (4) 3A=6S+42 \end{align} and equation <imath>(3)</imath> by <imath>-2</imath> to get \begin{align}(5) -2A=6T-104 \end{align} Add (4) and (5) to get <imath>A=6(S+T)-62</imath>. After substituting equation (1) and simplifying, you get <imath>A=\boxed{28}</imath> or answer choice <imath>\boxed{A}</imath>.

~PandaGod7even
